note: row - col and row + col identify the two diagonals in O(1), same trick as Python, now via unordered_set.
Swap-based permutation generation needs no visited array, mirroring the Python in-place version.
Half-open [lo, hi) with lo = mid + 1 is the C++ mirror of the same invariant as the Python version.
std::lower_bound and std::upper_bound are the C++ standard library's binary_search primitives.
insert returns the (possibly new) subtree root, which is how the caller reattaches it in one line.
The same fewest-coins recurrence as Python, with an explicit sentinel instead of a Python float infinity.
Same downward-capacity trick as the Python version prevents an item being reused within one round.
The 2D table indexes a[i-1] and b[j-1] because row and column 0 represent the empty prefix.
vector<vector<int>> adjacency is the idiomatic C++ graph, indexed by plain node id.
BFS over an unweighted adjacency list gives shortest paths, same guarantee as the Python version.
A pair<distance, node> in a min-heap priority_queue with std::greater is C++'s Dijkstra idiom.
A vector<int> parent array with path compression is the standard C++ DSU, no allocation per union.
Sorting by start then extending-or-opening is the same one-pass rule as the Python version.
priority_queue with std::greater is a min-heap; the C++ mirror of Python's heapq default.
Cycle detection needs raw pointers, not unique_ptr, since the structure is not tree-shaped.
Ownership walks forward via unique_ptr while a raw Node* trails behind as a non-owning cursor.
A list plus an unordered_map of iterators gives O(1) get and put with true recency order.
The <= in the merge step is what keeps the sort stable, exactly as in the Python version.
Each index is pushed and popped once with a vector-as-stack, same amortised linear bound as Python.
A length n+1 prefix vector removes the index-zero special case, same as the Python version.
Same one-pass Lomuto partition as the Python version, using std::swap on vector elements.
A vector<vector<int>>-adjacent structure here is the frequency map; grow right, shrink left.
A plain queue<Node*> over non-owning pointers is the natural BFS frontier in C++.
Owning the children via unique_ptr means the whole tree frees itself when the root goes out of scope.
Same sum-driven pointer movement as the Python version, now over an iterator-free index pair.
